🇲🇽📊 <u>CEPAL says Mexico is "trapped in low growth since 1990" — that is, since neoliberalism</u>

CEPAL cut Mexico's 2026 growth forecast to 1.3%, a third straight year below the regional average of 2.2%. But read the fine print: the UN body's own secretary general, Salazar-Xirinachs, dates the "low-growth trap" to 1990 — the dawn of the neoliberal era, decades before the 4T. And while CEPAL frets over the GDP line, the peso sits at its strongest since 2024, formal IMSS jobs hit a record 22.76 million, and 13.4 million Mexicans climbed out of poverty in six years. Growth measured the old way was never the point — distribution is.

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>Mexico's right-wing PAN just lost its registration in Coahuila</u>

The PAN — Mexico's main conservative party for decades — collapsed to roughly 2.1% in Coahuila's 2026 local election: no seats in the state Congress and its local registration wiped out entirely. The party that spent years playing junior partner to the PRI can no longer hold the ground it once dominated. El Soberano reads it as a marker of the right's disintegration heading into 2027.
banner: PAN LOSES ITS REGISTRATION IN COAHUILA

text:
🔥🇲🇽 <u>How Mexico's secret police groomed Salinas for the 1988 stolen election</u>

Mexico's political police — the DGIPS and the DFS, merged in 1985 and reborn as Cisen in 1989 — tracked Carlos Salinas de Gortari from 1982 to 1988, filling the national archives with hundreds of intelligence cards logging his cabinet meetings, regional tours and deals with governors, bosses and union chiefs. By 1987 the surveillance shifted from activity logs to biographical profiling, cataloguing his Harvard résumé in "documents meant to explain who this figure was" — the repression apparatus quietly prepping the architect of Mexican neoliberalism for the fraud-tainted presidency he would seize in 1988. Contralínea.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>The PRI's secret police spied on everyone — and badged a narco kingpin</u>

Declassified files show the DFS — the PRI regime's political police, created in 1947 with an explicit mandate to "surveil, control, detain and exterminate dissident groups and movements" — kept watch on presidents, muralist David Alfaro Siqueiros, journalist Julio Scherer, and a 16-year-old Claudia Sheinbaum (a January 1979 file logged her travels). Her mother, scientist Annie Pardo, was flagged "communist" for 1968. The same agency that hunted the left issued an official badge to drug lord Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo. Contralínea, straight from the national archives.
banner: PRI SECRET POLICE SPIED ON EVERYONE

text:
🇲🇽🚠 <u>Sheinbaum's cable car for the poor: "the best transport for those who have least"</u>

Mexico City's Cablebús Line 4 — 11 km, 9 stations, roughly 400 cabins, 65,000 riders a day — is 20% built and on track for December 2027, halving the commute from the southern hills down to Metro Universidad to 40 minutes. It's federally funded at over 4.7 billion pesos. "It's a social justice project, dedicated precisely to those who have the least — the best transport for those who have the least," said President Sheinbaum on site. Public infrastructure aimed downward, not at the wealthy.
banner: CABLEBUS L4: TRANSPORT FOR THE POOR

text:
🇲🇽🤖 <u>Public-school kids from Mexico just won the robotics world title in Japan</u>

Four students from Conalep Silao — a free public technical high school in Guanajuato — built a fully autonomous sumo robot and took first place worldwide at RoboRAVE International in Osaka, beating teams from across the planet in the 3-kg category. Team "Mantarraya" had placed only third nationally, refused to settle, and came back to top the world. This is what free public education builds.
banner: CONALEP: ROBOTICS WORLD TITLE IN JAPAN

People in the mountains lose up to two hours each way getting to work; now they'll spend that time with their families instead." — Claudia Sheinbaum, supervising Cablebús Line 4 — Aug 23, 2026 Line 4 will link Tlalpan and Coyoacán to Ciudad Universitaria: 9 stations, 11 km, 390 cabins, cutting the hilltop-to-Metro Universidad commute to 40 minutes — half the current time. Cost: 4.7 billion pesos, finished 2027. Mexico City's three existing cable-car lines already carry 40 million trips a year.

text: 🇲🇽🔍 US officials keep claiming Mexico “does nothing” on the cartels. Here is one weekend’s ledger. In Sinaloa, federal forces seized more than 8,000 rounds of ammunition and 172 improvised explosive devices, and dismantled a drug lab — across the municipalities of Concordia, Mazatlán and Culiacán. Enforcement carried out by Mexican forces, under Mexican command — not on orders from a foreign agency. — La Jornada, Aug 22, 2026

🚨🇲🇽 A former US DEA chief is now publicly ordering Mexico’s security cabinet to arrest an elected governor — and ship him to New York. On Aug 22, Derek Maltz, ex-acting head of the DEA, demanded that Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch “arrest and deport” Sinaloa governor Rubén Rocha Moya to the United States. Whatever the case against any official, one thing isn’t Washington’s to decide. Investigations run through Mexico’s own prosecutor, under Mexican law, on Mexican soil. A retired US agent does not issue orders to a sovereign country. — Infobae, Aug 22, 2026

🇲🇽📊 <u>Mexico's 2027 Budget: No New Taxes, Smaller Deficit</u>

Analysts and Hacienda point to a 2027 economic package with no new taxes — leaning on tighter SAT enforcement instead — and a fiscal deficit targeted at 3.5% of GDP, down from the 4.1% expected to close 2026. Treasury chief Edgar Amador calls the country's debt "adequate and manageable"; the package must reach Congress by Sept 8.
